proposed_from.topic: Post-selection-valid welfare–divergence frontier bands for benchmark-centered assignment rules. In an iid bounded-outcome causal model with overlap, finitely many actions, and a fixed finite-dimensional benchmark-centered softmax class, index the best rule by a KL preference c in a positive compact interval. Assume a unique uniformly interior optimizer with a uniformly negative Hessian and cross-fitted doubly robust nuisance conditions. Prove a joint uniform influence expansion and Gaussian limit for the optimizer, welfare, and benchmark-divergence paths, consistently estimate the covariance kernel, and validate a conditional multiplier bootstrap. Construct a simultaneous confidence tube for the two-coordinate welfare–divergence frontier that remains valid after any measurable choice of c from the plotted curve; use set-valued inversion at tangencies or self-intersections. Jointly calibrate the n-scaled penalized-regret process through its Hessian quadratic form. Credit Fang–Ridder–Xie arXiv:2512.19230v3 for fixed-preference efficiency and their three-arm commitment-savings frontier. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The score-blind presolve derived the joint influence maps for the optimizer, welfare, and divergence, the penalized cancellation identity, and the uniform quadratic-regret reduction. It solved the binary-covariate three-action witness exactly, established a uniform curvature lower bound 0.0026816936, and numerically checked influence centering and frontier derivatives. Vanishing penalties, weak overlap, redundant logits, localization, selected-index limits, constrained inversion, estimated scale, and oracle-versus-implemented welfare were checked; generic indexed-inference results cap novelty but no exact collision was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove conditional multiplier replacement and tightness for fold-specific estimated stacked influences evaluated along the same-sample optimizer path, using shrinking empirical-L2 error and uniform entropy bounds. EARLY KILL TEST: On the twelve-atom witness at c=.5,1,2, verify influence centering, penalized cancellation, H theta-prime=-grad K, and the quadratic regret expansion, then check held-out nuisance linearization and multiplier covariance errors; a persistent root-n remainder or failed identity stops the run. seed_details.title: Uniform orthogonal limit theory for the optimizer and welfare--divergence path
seed_details.anchor_receipt: The anchor was read at Sections 1--4, 7--8, Theorems 2 and 5, and their proofs. It fixes one positive preference coefficient, obtains a regular efficient optimizer and a pointwise quadratic-regret law, and plots rather than jointly infers the preference path. Its conclusion identifies data-driven preference choice as a later direction.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The fixed-preference proof first changes where pointwise cross-fitted remainder control must become uniform after the estimated foldwise influence map is composed with the same-sample optimizer path.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for benchmark-centered softmax multiplier bootstraps, causal welfare--divergence confidence tubes, and cross-fitted optimizer-path processes found generic indexed orthogonal bands but no theorem for this stacked composition.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from BelloniChernozhukovChetverikovWei2018 because their uniform Bahadur and estimated-score multiplier theorems already cover function-valued orthogonal targets.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their generic theorem supplies the last approximation layer, but the random fold-specific class evaluated at an implicit same-sample argmax is not one of their verified applications; the publishable delta is a complete verification plus the optimizer, welfare, divergence, and implemented-value stack for the anchor's policy model.

seed_details.title: A conditionally calibrated quadratic-regret process over all positive preferences
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Theorem 2 and its proof were read. The proof is a fixed-preference second-order Taylor expansion, while Theorem 5 inserts the efficient doubly robust optimizer limit. No pathwise regret process or simultaneous critical value is supplied.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is a uniform second-order expansion with one optimizer Gaussian process and one Hessian path, followed by a quadratic plug-in multiplier law rather than a naive recentered bootstrap.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search paired uniform policy regret with second-order bootstrap inference. ChenFang2019 gives the general degeneracy warning and correction principle, but no indexed causal-policy quadratic process was found.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from FangRidderXie2026 pointwise regret plus the continuous mapping theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: Uniform Taylor control and the quadratic map are routine only after the hard estimated-influence path bootstrap has been proved; as a standalone result this is too incremental, so it is retained only as a second theorem coupled to the uniform frontier process.

seed_details.title: Local-to-zero preference phase diagram between regular softmax and hard treatment choice
seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction, Section 3, Section 5, and Conclusion were read. The paper explicitly separates fixed positive penalties from the nonregular zero-penalty boundary; uniform Hessian inversion is the first regular proof step that fails as the coefficient vanishes.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Replace uniform curvature by a local eigenvalue sequence and derive the normalization at which softmax smoothing bias, optimizer noise, and hard-policy nonregularity balance.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing vanishing KL temperature with treatment-rule asymptotics found Hirano--Porter's hard-rule endpoint and Crippa's smoothing-dependent threshold-policy regret, but no semiparametric transition for benchmark-centered assignment.
seed_details.red_team: A routine smoothing-parameter exercise combining the positive-penalty anchor with Crippa2025.
seed_details.rebuttal: The destination requires a new local experiment and a regime-dependent inverse-Hessian limit, not a substitution into either endpoint theorem; feasibility is nevertheless too uncertain for the first version.

seed_details.title: Semiparametric efficiency for the full preference-indexed frontier
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Section 3 and Theorem 5 were read. The paper derives the efficient influence function and attainable covariance for each fixed preference, but it does not formulate an efficiency ordering for confidence tubes or the full path as a Banach-valued parameter.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to define regularity and convolution bounds for the path in a function space rather than at finitely many deterministic coordinates.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for semiparametric efficiency bounds for policy-frontier confidence tubes found pointwise efficiency and generic functional inference, but no useful pathwise Loewner-minimal kernel or optimal-width theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Pointwise efficiency at every preference automatically gives efficiency of the path.
seed_details.rebuttal: That implication does not by itself order nonlinear tube widths, while a Banach-space convolution theorem may be formal rather than decision-relevant; the seed is dropped until an optimal confidence-loss criterion is identified.

seed_details.title: Matched minimax rates for the frontier under deteriorating overlap
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Assumption 2 and the efficiency calculations were read. The anchor requires support and integrability at a fixed preference and does not study a sequence of observational propensities approaching zero.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is the influence-envelope bound: inverse propensities now grow with a primitive overlap exponent, changing both upper rates and least-favorable perturbations.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for weak-overlap minimax policy-frontier estimation found broad weak-overlap causal estimation but no matched rate for the KL optimizer and its bivariate frontier.
seed_details.red_team: This is generic weak-overlap theory with a softmax label.
seed_details.rebuttal: A genuinely new result would require a coupled lower bound for the optimizer and frontier geometry; the current substrate does not yet isolate that reduction, so the seed is dropped rather than padded.

seed_details.title: Choose a benchmark-proximity preference by a reporting-guarantee rule
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Section 2.2 and the Conclusion were read. The coefficient is a planner preference rather than a tuning parameter, and the paper reports its path without a data-driven selection rule.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to optimize a simultaneous lower confidence functional over the preference path and compare its welfare to an oracle preference subject to a divergence budget.
seed_details.destination_search: PolicyLearningWithConfidence2026 was opened through its current public manuscript. Its propositions already give reporting guarantees and regret bounds for confidence-penalized policy selection across a general policy set.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from PolicyLearningWithConfidence2026 by taking the policy set to be the softmax frontier.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for the broad selection theorem; without a KL-specific sharper oracle relation, this seed is occupied and is dropped.

seed_details.title: Set-valued inversion of the welfare--divergence tube
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Section 2.2 was read. It warns that divergence in a restricted class need not be one-to-one in the preference. Direct differentiation in the maintained identifiable softmax model, however, gives a nonincreasing divergence path.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step from RenTelschowSchwartzman2024 is inversion of a bivariate optimizer-generated band without choosing a local inverse branch.
seed_details.destination_search: RenTelschowSchwartzman2024 Theorem 1 was read and already turns simultaneous bands into simultaneous inner and outer inverse sets. YamazoeNaito2024 treats an embedded curve, not optimizer-generated values.
seed_details.red_team: Band inversion is an eventwise set inclusion, and the regular softmax path cannot genuinely self-intersect.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection defeats this as a standalone kernel. The construction remains a useful corollary because it avoids derivative division at a constant path or finite-sample near-tangency.

seed_details.title: Uniform frontier inference after adaptive experimental assignment
seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Introduction and related-literature discussion were read. They motivate adaptive experiments but expressly restrict the analysis to data from a fixed benchmark.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step replaces the i.i.d. empirical-process expansion by a uniform martingale-array expansion with predictable variance depending on both the preference and adaptive logging probabilities.
seed_details.destination_search: HadadEtAl2021 was opened and supplies variance-stabilized AIPW confidence intervals for fixed policy values under adaptive experiments; adaptive policy-learning papers supply regret but no joint optimizer-frontier tube.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate by applying HadadEtAl2021 pointwise over a compact one-dimensional index.
seed_details.rebuttal: Uniform predictable covariance, optimization, and estimated-path replacement are not pointwise consequences, but the change of sampling model is too large for this fixed-i.i.d. version.

seed_details.title: Finite-sample randomization inversion for a selected frontier point
seed_details.anchor_receipt: The fixed-benchmark experimental interpretation in Sections 1--2 was read. Its welfare target integrates heterogeneous potential outcomes under counterfactual rules rather than testing a sharp constant-effect null.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step would require a symmetry orbit that imputes the missing potential outcomes needed to recompute the learned frontier under assignment permutations.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing randomization or conformal inversion with learned welfare frontiers found symmetry methods for sharp counterfactual nulls, but no exact orbit for this composite heterogeneous-policy target.
seed_details.red_team: No exact finite-sample randomization distribution exists for the weak welfare null without additional effect restrictions.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds in the maintained model, so the required M17 lane has no credible survivor and is explicitly dropped.
